title: Sequence of invasive cardiac care pathways for patients with chronic heart failure, atrial fibrillation and mitral valve insufficiency
summary:
The INCEPTION-PILOT study examines the interaction between atrial fibrillation and mitral valve leakage (also known as mitral valve regurgitation). These two conditions share a common structure in the heart, namely the left atrium. The interplay between the two conditions is not well understood, either clinically or scientifically. In routine clinical practice, there is currently no treatment concept for patients with heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and mitral valve regurgitation requiring treatment if they are no longer amenable to cardiac surgery.
Therefore, we are conducting a clinical study investigating the impact of the sequence of minimally invasive therapies (also known as pulmonary vein isolation for the treatment of atrial fibrillation and mitral valve clip therapy). The focus lies on the quality of life of the participating patients.
conditions: Heart failure, mitral valve insufficiency, atrial fibrillation, interventional therapy, edge-to-edge repair, pulmonary vein isolation

interventions.name: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) followed by transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the mitral valve (M-TEER)
Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the mitral valve (M-TEER) followed by pulmonary vein isolation (PVI)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation with indication for pulmonary vein isolation.
- Mitral valve insufficiency (predominantly functional etiology) requiring treatment with indication for catheter-based repair
- NYHA ≥ II
Exclusion criteria:
- Significant language barrier
- Previous pulmonary vein isolation within the last 3 months
- Left atrial appendage thrombus
- Serious contraindications to oral anticoagulant therapy
- Patients with acute myocardial infarction, elective coronary intervention, cardiac surgery, or pacemaker implantation one month prior to the first planned procedure according to the study protocol.
- Walking distance < 50 m within the 6 minute walking distance test
